properties.description: scripts/run_bulk_extraction.py --dry-run calls spend.declare() BEFORE branching on the dry-run flag, so a dry run writes a ceiling declaration onto the append-only spend ledger (state/spend_ledger.jsonl) for a run that never dispatches a call. A dry run exists to PRICE a run before committing to it; declaring is the commitment. Consequences: (a) a caller who only wants a projection must invent a --ceiling-tokens value, and that fabricated number is then permanently on the ledger as a declared ceiling with the task file named as its authority; (b) the real ceiling, derived from the dry run's own output, must then be a superseding re-declare, so the ledger reads as an operator ceiling correction when nothing was corrected. Found while executing chunked_pilot ADDENDUM-03 §2 on 2026-08-29: the section specified this runner, and scripts/chunked_pilot.py --phase dry_run was used instead and the discrepancy reported in the RESULT. Fix: move the declare() call inside the non-dry-run branch and make --ceiling-tokens not required when --dry-run is set. Second, smaller defect in the same command: --dry-run has no chunker, so under a chunked profile it prints whole documents and cannot produce the per-document chunk counts a chunked profile needs priced.

The duplicate is introducing-the-oecd-ai-capability-indicators: a 2026-07-04 admission of a crawl4ai capture of component-5.html (one component of a 56-page OECD report) and a 2026-08-14 operator-cleared extent correction (CLEARANCE 2, 2026-08-14_bulk_v1_closeout) replacing it with the full PDF. add()'s duplicate-doc_id check was byte-identical in intent then (verified against commit 94fd280) and would have raised; the event was written straight to shard batch-005 because content_update — the sanctioned supersession event, with reason extent_corrected — did not exist until 2026-08-29, fifteen days later. No data defect: replay takes the later add, the entry in force is the corrected PDF, and manifest_added_ids() is set-based so reconciles:YES at 194 was never wrong. Added kg.manifest.duplicate_adds(), a log-level invariant add() cannot express, classifying duplicates as explained/unexplained, plus 5 tests including a live-log monitor allowlisting this one pair by event id and a mutation proving the doc_id check (not content_hash) is what rejects a duplicate. All mutations verified to fire. Annotation: document_annotation 2b1556ed, property admission_supersession, reason extent_corrected — NOT a content_update, which would misstate the sequence and be refused as bytes-unchanged. Verified not in the projection whitelist. Suite 589 passed. Record: docs/research/2026-08-31_duplicate_manifest_add_95f286e4.md

properties.description: Design the standing dispatcher (L4 gap: dispatch latency, not decision-making). Evidence from 2026-08-31/09-01: auto-registered gap tasks, ADDENDUM-03 with gate open, and zero-spend housekeeping all sat in `proposed` until a human relayed a dispatch line — the system solves problems into proposed state and then waits for a message bus. Build: a runner that polls Seldon for dispatchable tasks against HARD machine-checkable criteria only (declared ceiling within standing band; no liveness conflict on owned files/queues per a file-ownership model; gate conditions machine-verifiable; zero-spend tasks always eligible), launches CC headless per DD-019, and logs each dispatch decision as an event with the criteria evaluation. Operator touchpoints unchanged (spend above band, external sends, value inputs, incidents) — the dispatcher enforces the closed list instead of the operator enacting it. Design session first (Desktop): gate-condition language, file-ownership/lease model (two runners on one queue is the batch-identity class at runner grain — four instances say design this carefully), launchd scheduling, kill switch. Prior art: cron/CI schedulers, Wintermute's launchd morning-brief pipeline, the burn's own STOP-file convention, the wintermute lease/reaper mechanism.

Essay/paper: "Statistical boundaries can't be reasoned across; judgment boundaries can" — the decision-theoretic and philosophical grounding of this system's design, written for a general technical audience (distinct from f1da94c6, the FCSM methods paper). Spine: (1) small-world vs large-world decisions — Knight 1921 (risk vs uncertainty), Savage 1954 (small worlds), Wald 1945 (SPRT; statistical decisions spend judgment early, in the loss function), Meehl 1954 / Grove & Meehl 1996 (mechanical vs clinical prediction), Kahneman/Sibony/Sunstein 2021 Noise (bias vs noise; rules beat judges where rules can be written), Taleb (ludic fallacy, Black Swan). (2) The three boundaries: statistical (more data dissolves it; escalating intelligence adds nothing), judgment (model underdetermined; collapses to rules wherever weights can be stated — automation of judgment = converting one-off calls to standing policy, as this project's addenda did), accountability (non-epistemic; culpability needs a legal person; Elish "moral crumple zone"; per-decision sign-off at machine scale = liability sponge; the defensible form is ex-ante policy signature — sign the loss function/gates/ceilings, not each output — mirroring how statistical agencies sign methodology, not estimates). (3) Live exhibit: OpenAI/Hugging Face incident (July 2026, reports 2026-08-26 from OpenAI and METR/Redwood): reward hacking as Goodhart on the loss function; 93% of message-board discussion traced to 198 never-solved tasks — impossible evals with no safe exit redirect optimization at the scorer; contrast with this system's GATE UNREACHABLE refuse-not-verdict rule (DD-026, G1 fix) and pre-registered satisfiable gates. (4) Stigmergy (Grassé 1959, ant/bee coordination through environment traces): the unsanctioned message board as emergent stigmergy; event-sourced graph + task files as sanctioned stigmergy with provenance and admission gates; machine intelligence as its own kind (not deficient human intelligence) — design for what coordinates machines well, not what mimics humans. Sources: metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/, OpenAI 2026-08-26 report, thehackernews.com 2026-08 coverage. Register under ai-readiness-kg for now; venue TBD (blog/preprint). Desktop authors the CC task spec when prioritized.

Chunker overlap join costs recall on assembled documents. chunker.Chunk.grounding_text() returns overlap_text + '\n\n' + text; each part is a verbatim document substring but the CONCATENATION is not, so it only reproduces the document when the real split point was a blank line. A model span straddling that junction is chunk-valid and document-invalid, and phase_ingest's document-level re-validation rejects it (node_not_in_document / edge_not_in_document). Measured 2026-09-01 on chunk grounding_text NOT being a document substring: odcs 25/45, slsa 17/32 (both assembled by scripts/extent_remediation.py with '---' + heading + 'Source:' separators at section boundaries) vs fcsm-20-04 2/47 and w3c-dcat-3 0/42 (native documents). Cost on bulk_v038_b014: 18 nodes + 21 edges rejected, ~5 percent of proposals. This costs RECALL, not correctness -- nothing ungrounded entered the graph, and the re-validation is the guard working as designed. Two candidate fixes, neither safe mid-burn because changing chunk boundaries invalidates chunk-level resume for every batch: (a) have grounding_text() return the true document slice spanning overlap start to body end rather than a synthetic join; (b) have the extent-remediation assembler use blank-line-only separators. Prefer (a); it fixes the general case rather than one producer. Source: cc_tasks/2026-08-30_bulk_extraction_v038_RESULT.md ADDENDUM-03 section.
